newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-NDETI, LORUPE FAVORED TO WIN N.Y. MARATHON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-NDETI, LORUPE FAVORED TO WIN N.Y. MARATHON.

text.p: Kenyans Cosmas Ndeti and Telga Lorupe, who is looking for her third consecutive women's victory, are favoured to win the 20th New York City Marathon on Sunday.

Some 29,000 runners, looking to capture the $30,000 first-place prize, a new luxury automobile and a healthy measure of fame, are expected to start the 26.2 mile (42 km) course that winds its way through the city's five boroughs.

Competing here for the first time, Ndeti is seeking to avenge his loss to fellow-Kenyan Moses Tanui at the Boston Marathon in April that spoiled his bid for a unprecedented fourth-consecutive victory.
"This is the rematch," Ndeti said of lining up against Tanu, who clocked a personal best of two hours, nine minutes and 16 seconds at Boston, while Ndeti finished third.
"I trust in my training and trust in my God," said Ndeti. "I'm going to do something Sunday. I'm ready to win.
Race director Allan Steinfeld said he lkes Ndeti's chances to be the first Kenyan to win the men's division since Ibrahim Hussein in 1987.
"I'm putting my money on him," Steinfeld said of the 24-year-old Kenyan. "I'm hoping that after his lost in Boston that he is very hungry to show the world that he is the man."

The challengers includes two former New York Marathon champions from Mexico -- 1993 winner Andres Espinosa and Salvador Garcia, who won in 1991. Also entered is Martin Fiz of Spain, who finished fourth at the Atlanta Olympics and another Kenyan, Ezekiel Bitok, second at Boston this year.
Two-time defending champion German Silva is not running. The Mexican decided to rest after struggling to a sixth place finish at the Olympics.
"I feel a little bit sad, I'm not competing this time," said Silva. "I would like to be back very much next year."
Lorupe, 22, has run away from the fields the last two year, winning by margins of more than two minutes, to become the first repeat woman's winner since Waitz won five in a row from 1982-86.
"When I come to New York, I feel like I am coming home," said Loroupe, who was leading at Boston this year through 25 miles before cramping and finishing second to Uta Pippig of Germany.

Lorupe is expected to be challenged by American Kim Jones, the 1989 and '90 runner-up, and Italian Franca Fiacconi, who has won five of her last six marathons, including a victory at Capri just three weeks ago.

A late entry sure to attract fan curiosity, but not expected to contend for the victory, is masters runner 40-year-old Norwegian Ingrid Kristiansen, who still holds the world record of 2:21:06 set in 1985 at London. Kristiansen is the 1989 NY champion.
